# package-trends

> npm download trends as a sparkline, a calendar heatmap, a line of text, or a KPI block. Compare packages, repair npm's missing days. Zero dependencies, works without a proxy.

A package's npm downloads as a sparkline, a line of text or a KPI block. Zero dependencies, a framework-agnostic core and React components. It fetches straight from the npm registry, which needs no key and sends a permissive CORS header, so no proxy is involved.

- Version 0.2.0, MIT, © Plain Matter Pte Ltd.
- Install: `npm i package-trends`
- Source: https://github.com/tbudin/package-trends
- Every page below is also available as markdown at its URL plus `index.md`.
- The whole documentation as one file: https://tbudin.github.io/package-trends/llms-full.txt

## Start

- [package-trends: download trends small enough for a footer](https://tbudin.github.io/package-trends/index.md): Install package-trends and draw a package's npm downloads as a sparkline, a line of text or a KPI block — no dependencies, no stylesheet, no chart library.

## Variants

- [Sparkline](https://tbudin.github.io/package-trends/sparkline/index.md): The default variant: shape only, no axes and no labels, sized for a nav, a list row or a table cell.
- [Text](https://tbudin.github.io/package-trends/text/index.md): The text variant: the count, the word and the change on one line, inheriting the colour of the sentence it sits in.
- [KPI](https://tbudin.github.io/package-trends/kpi/index.md): The KPI variant: a tile where the number leads, the change qualifies it and a small chart shows the number is not a fluke.

## Charts

- [Curves](https://tbudin.github.io/package-trends/curves/index.md): How the line joins its points: linear, step, or monotone cubic smoothing that can never draw a count that never happened.
- [Columns](https://tbudin.github.io/package-trends/column/index.md): Discrete days as columns anchored at zero, with weekly or monthly bucketing for packages busy enough that thirty bars look identical.
- [Bands](https://tbudin.github.io/package-trends/band/index.md): Each bucket's low, mean and high drawn as a range — the honest alternative to a candlestick, which a daily count cannot fill.
- [Marks and axis](https://tbudin.github.io/package-trends/marks/index.md): Calling out the last point, the peak or the trough, and when a rule at zero is worth drawing at all.

## Scale

- [Size](https://tbudin.github.io/package-trends/size/index.md): Sizing a chart in pixels, in em so it scales with the text it sits in, or fluid so it fills its container.
- [Domain](https://tbudin.github.io/package-trends/domain/index.md): The y-range values are laid out across, and why two charts side by side are only comparable on a fixed one.

## Data

- [Periods and smoothing](https://tbudin.github.io/package-trends/periods/index.md): Named periods and explicit date ranges, weekly and monthly bucketing, and why smoothing never touches the figures beside the chart.
- [Gaps in npm's data](https://tbudin.github.io/package-trends/gaps/index.md): npm answers 0 for a day it has not aggregated, indistinguishable from a real zero. What that does to the figures, and the repair.
- [analyse()](https://tbudin.github.io/package-trends/analyse/index.md): Growth, linear fit and r², weekday profile, weekend ratio, volatility, spikes and streak — the figures behind a sentence about a package.

## Compare

- [Comparing packages](https://tbudin.github.io/package-trends/compare/index.md): Several packages on one chart, on an absolute scale or indexed against their own start, and the spread figure that tells you which to use.

## Using it

- [On the server](https://tbudin.github.io/package-trends/server/index.md): Fetch once where the page is built and pass the range down, so no visitor costs a request and the chart is in the first paint.
- [Styling](https://tbudin.github.io/package-trends/styling/index.md): No stylesheet ships. The chart strokes in currentColor and sets its type in em, so it inherits a host's palette instead of imposing one.
- [Accessibility](https://tbudin.github.io/package-trends/accessibility/index.md): Every chart carries a sentence for a screen reader, the sign always accompanies the colour, and a failed fetch renders nothing rather than breaking a footer.

## Reference

- [Every option](https://tbudin.github.io/package-trends/reference/index.md): The full surface: every prop on the components, every export of the core, and what each of the 4 entry points costs.

## Releases
